slides.heading: Reception — Autumn 1, Week 4
slides.sub: New sounds taught directly, practised and applied in words, captions and the matching decodable book.

slides.heading: Mon
slides.objective: Learn the new sound "g" (/ɡ/) and start reading and spelling words that use it.

slides.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" width="320" height="320" role="img" aria-label="goat" class="wp-icon wp-raster" data-picture="goat"><image href="data:image/png;base64, " x="0" y="0" width="100" height="100" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"/></svg>

slides.mnemonic: Gigi the egg wobbles gently from side to side — 'g, g, g' — rocking but never falling.

character.name: Gigi
character.blurb: Gigi is a speckled egg tucked safely in a nest, who loves to rock gently from side to side.

slides.pronunciation_note: A soft sound made at the back of the throat — 'g' as in 'got', not 'guh'.
slides.formation_cue: Start at the top right of a small round shape. Curve round to the left and back up to where you started, then go straight down below the line and curl round to the left. Finish below the line.
slides.formation_rhyme: Round like a, then a long tail.
slides.action: Rock gently from side to side on the spot, like Gigi wobbling in her nest, saying 'g, g'.
slides.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" width="320" height="320" role="img" aria-label="goat" class="wp-icon wp-raster" data-picture="goat"><image href="data:image/png;base64, " x="0" y="0" width="100" height="100" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"/></svg>

slides.tip: You'll spot 'the' everywhere in a story — the tricky bit is the ending, which says a quick 'thuh' instead of the 'eh' sound e usually makes.

slides.heading: Tue
slides.objective: Learn the new sound "o" (/ɒ/) and start reading and spelling words that use it.

slides.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" width="320" height="320" role="img" aria-label="orange" class="wp-icon wp-raster" data-picture="orange"><image href="data:image/png;base64," x="0" y="0" width="100" height="100" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"/></svg>

slides.mnemonic: Ozzy the owl opens his big round eyes wide and hoots — 'o, o, o'.

character.name: Ozzy
character.blurb: Ozzy is a round-eyed owl with two little feather tufts, who blinks slowly and loves the quiet of night.

slides.pronunciation_note: A short, round sound made with rounded lips — 'o' as in 'dog', not the long letter name.
slides.formation_cue: Start at the top. Curve round to the left, down, round the bottom and back up. Finish where you started, closing the circle.
slides.formation_rhyme: Round the circle, back to the start.
slides.action: Make two round circles with your thumbs and fingers and hold them up to your eyes like Ozzy's, saying 'o, o'.
slides.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" width="320" height="320" role="img" aria-label="orange" class="wp-icon wp-raster" data-picture="orange"><image href="data:image/png;base64," x="0" y="0" width="100" height="100" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"/></svg>

slides.heading: Wed
slides.objective: Learn the new sound "c" (/k/) and start reading and spelling words that use it.

slides.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" width="320" height="320" role="img" aria-label="cat" class="wp-icon wp-raster" data-picture="cat"><image href="data:image/png;base64," x="0" y="0" width="100" height="100" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"/></svg>

slides.mnemonic: Coco the caterpillar curls up small on a leaf — 'c, c, c' — curling a little tighter each time.

character.name: Coco
character.blurb: Coco is a striped caterpillar who loves to curl into a tight little ball whenever she feels shy.

slides.pronunciation_note: A short, sharp sound from the back of the throat — 'c' as in 'cat', not 'cuh'.
slides.formation_cue: Start at the top right. Curve up, over to the left, round and down. Finish at the bottom right, leaving the c open.
slides.formation_rhyme: Curve left around, leave it open.
slides.action: Curl one hand slowly into a loose fist, like Coco curling up, saying a short 'c'.
slides.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" width="320" height="320" role="img" aria-label="cat" class="wp-icon wp-raster" data-picture="cat"><image href="data:image/png;base64," x="0" y="0" width="100" height="100" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"/></svg>

slides.heading: Thu
slides.objective: Learn the new sound "k" (/k/) and start reading and spelling words that use it.

slides.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" width="320" height="320" role="img" aria-label="kite" class="wp-icon wp-raster" data-picture="kite"><image href="data:image/png;base64," x="0" y="0" width="100" height="100" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"/></svg>

slides.mnemonic: Kip the acorn lands on the path and cracks his cap with a sharp little click — 'k, k, k'.

character.name: Kip
character.blurb: Kip is a fresh acorn who has just fallen from the tree, and his cap always clicks when he lands.

slides.pronunciation_note: The same sharp sound as 'c' — a quick, short 'k', not 'kuh'.
slides.formation_cue: Start at the top of a tall line and pull straight down. Finish on the line. Lift, start at the top right of the small letters, slant in to touch the tall line, then slant out. Finish on the line.
slides.formation_rhyme: Straight down, two legs meet halfway.
slides.action: Tap one knuckle sharply on the table or your knee once, like Kip's cap cracking, saying 'k'.
slides.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" width="320" height="320" role="img" aria-label="kite" class="wp-icon wp-raster" data-picture="kite"><image href="data:image/png;base64," x="0" y="0" width="100" height="100" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"/></svg>

slides.heading: Fri
slides.objective: Revisit everything taught this week, read the matched decodable book, and check how securely it has been learned.
